newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil govt sees 4.5-5.0 pct GDP growth in '97.
newsitem.headline: Brazil govt sees 4.5-5.0 pct GDP growth in '97.

text.p: The Brazilian government expects 3.0 percent gross domestic product growth for 1996 and between 4.5-5.0 percent growth in 1997, presidential spokesman Sergio Amaral said.
Amaral said Finance Minister Pedro Malan had presented the growth estimates to President Fernando Henrique Cardoso and his ministers at a special cabinet meeting on Saturday.
Amaral said GDP growth in the third quarter of 1996 was 6.5 percent.
"We have arrived in the second half of 1996 with an acceleration in economic activity which will guarantee 3.0 percent growth this year and next year 4.5-5.0 percent," he said.
Amaral said Malan had pointed out to the cabinet that GDP growth from 1993 to 1998 will have been almost 30 percent, putting Brazil on track for a trillion-dollar GDP by the year 2001.
Malan gave lower estimates for 1997 in a Reuters interview in mid-November, projecting GDP growth of 3.5-4.0 percent.
